data.body:
Implementation pushed as Gerrit change 2074 (Change-Id If74eaa404c261ae0049633844b40482c866a0bef).

Verification of the plan's claims against the tree before review (all confirmed):
- The duplication is real and byte-identical: failure.py:148-157 vs sizing.py:316-329.
- AC greps run clean on the pre-change tree and discriminate: 'too many tokens' hit exactly
  {failure.py, sizing.py}; 'maximum context length' hit ONLY completion_failures.py:78 (the
  vacuous-AC finding is confirmed, and the corrected AC no longer has that defect).
- orchestrator.py:72 does bind _is_context_limit_error = sizing.is_context_limit_error at import
  time, and test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:45 monkeypatches the name as a string, so
  the def had to survive in sizing.
- Bug injurious-definable-badger's description does say 'Leave check_response's raise text
  unchanged (already accurate)', confirming the structured.py merge was decided against.
- No import cycle: failure.py imports only rebar.llm.errors.

file_impact was corrected from the withdrawn seven-file list to the three files actually touched;
that was also why the prior attestation kept going stale on unrelated _cli/_commands churn.
Title changed to match the delivered scope (the E3 advisory); title is not review material, so
the PASS attestation stayed certified.

Mutation evidence for the new tests (each perturbation restored afterwards):
- restore sizing's local tuple -> the uniqueness guard AND the live-read behaviour test go RED
  (this was the initial RED run);
- drop 'prompt is too long' from the owner tuple -> uniqueness guard + the verdict table go RED;
- scanner subset check -> intersection -> the partial-copy test goes RED;
- scanner never appends a hit -> three tests go RED;
- scanner ignores the escape marker -> the escape-marker test goes RED;
- match phrases as file substrings instead of AST string literals -> the prose test goes RED;
- drop the \S that makes the opt-out reason mandatory -> the escape-marker test goes RED;
- orchestrator stops aliasing the predicate -> the patchable-predicate test goes RED.
An earlier form of the reason rule survived mutation because two redundant checks masked each
other; the rule was single-sourced into the regex so the mutation now bites.
